subject: Request: On-prem latency attribution and SLA carveout
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@novaterra.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <agomez@novaterra.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem rollout: request for SLA carveout for customer-managed network

Jordan —

Thanks again for the onboarding call today. We've finished the initial rollout of Redwood Private (agent + VPC egress) in our staging region and are seeing intermittent token-generation latency spikes that line up with our VPN failover windows and some packet loss on the carrier link. Given that the traffic egress and firewall rules are managed by Novaterra, we need to ask Redwood for a formal carveout in the SLA for latency incidents attributable to customer-controlled networking.

What we're asking for:
- Temporary amendment language that exempts Redwood from latency SLOs when the cause is customer-controlled network elements (VPN gateways, carrier peering, or customer-side NAT).
- Acceptance criteria to establish attribution (traceroutes, packet captures, or your agent logs).
- A rollback/fallback policy so we can keep production traffic working while we troubleshoot.

Attached: a short network diagram and a troubleshooting log that shows the correlation. Happy to hop on a quick call — Alicia and I are in PST afternoons.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Infrastructure, Novaterra Systems
Attachments: novaterra_network_diag.pdf (diagram), troubleshooting_log_20270420.txt (text log)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@novaterra.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem rollout: request for SLA carveout for customer-managed network

Samir —

Appreciate the details and the attachments. Quick notes and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Attribution checklist — what we typically need to accept a carveout:
   - End-to-end traceroute + timestamps that show the tail latency originating in customer border network.
   - Any relevant firewall/NAT config snippets showing connection termination/conntrack timeouts.
   - Our agent logs (we'll share a signed snapshot) to match token timestamps.

2) Temporary amendment — we can draft a short appendix that:
   - Excludes Redwood from latency/throughput SLOs where the root cause is customer-managed network or carrier.
   - Requires reasonable cooperation (sharing traces/pcaps) for attribution.
   - Includes a 30-day review window and a mitigation plan (e.g., route via hosted fallback) while Novaterra remedies the carrier issues.

3) Mitigations to offer now:
   - Enable routed fallback to Redwood-hosted Dedicated for critical routes (we can failover traffic to Dedicated for specific model routes).
   - Increase prefix/KV caching for your most latency-sensitive paths to hide transient spikes.

I'll draft language and loop in Legal/Compliance if you want formal wording. Vivek & Neha — can you review the technical acceptance checklist and confirm whether Redwood needs any extra telemetry from Novaterra agent for attribution?

If Samir/Alicia are available, I can do a quick call Thu 4/22 PST.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Jordan —

Thanks — Thu afternoon PST works for us. I'm attaching a slightly expanded packet-trace excerpt and the carrier incident timeline (we've redacted a carrier ticket number). The logs show two notable events: a 20–40s VPN failover during which TCP retransmits spike, and a repeated NAT translation timeout that coincides with long tail token generation latency.

We agree with your proposed amendment bullets. Two asks from Novaterra:
- The carveout should explicitly call out carrier maintenance and customer-managed VPN appliances.
- We want an explicit rollback option: automatic routing to Redwood-hosted Dedicated for the affected route if attribution is confirmed.

Attachments: novaterra_network_diag.pdf (updated), troubleshooting_log_20270420.txt (expanded)

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: On-prem rollout: request for SLA carveout for customer-managed network

Team —

Summary and action items following Novaterra's ask: they want an explicit SLA appendix that:
- Exempts Redwood from latency SLO breaches where the root cause is customer-managed network (VPN appliances, carrier peering, on-prem NAT).
- Defines attribution evidence: traceroutes, signed agent logs, PCAPs, and carrier incident references.
- Allows automatic routing to Redwood-hosted Dedicated for affected routes once attribution is confirmed.

Proposal (high level):
1) Draft a short appendix (2–3 paragraphs) with carveout language that requires "reasonable cooperation" for attribution and a 30-day joint review window.
2) Add a procedural checklist for attribution (see Samir's notes).
3) Define the automated fallback: routing policy to Dedicated with an SLA transition window (e.g., immediate redirect + 72-hour remediation SLA for restoration).

Questions for Legal/Compliance: any red flags with the automated fallback clause? It effectively guarantees a hosted fallthrough for critical traffic — is that commercially acceptable without additional repo/credits?

Neha — Vivek — can you:
- Neha: draft the appendix language (attach as docx) and mark any legal toggles.
- Vivek: confirm agent telemetry we need and whether a signed snapshot plus traceroute is sufficient for engineering to accept attribution.

I'll propose the draft to Novaterra and include the DocuSign link once Legal signs off. Attached initial draft for your edit: draft-sla-amendment.docx

Thanks,
Jordan
